messages:
Jordan: Heads up — p95 on the latency dashboard jumped ~120ms for /v1/generate in prod after the routing policy rollout. Console view shows ~240ms, endpoint breakdown shows ~120ms. Anyone else seeing mismatched percentiles?
Emily: I noticed it too, started at ~02:12 UTC. My hunch: console is merging per-route tdigest differently than the endpoint breakdown which shows per-host pctl. Could be a merge/weighting issue or sampling origin tag.
Sam: Routing change went out at 1728888820, added fallback to quantized-small variant for heavy tails. That variant has higher tail and gets routed for slow callers — routing policy might change sample distribution.
Mike: Do we have sample counts? If console merges groups without stable weights we can get inflated p95. Also we had a bug last month where `route_fallback=true` lost the origin tag during rollups.
Emily: Quick query I ran in analytics to compare:
```
-- top-level per-host p95 for route
SELECT host, pctl(0.95, latency_ms) AS p95, count(*) AS n
FROM requests
WHERE route = 'generate' AND env = 'prod'
GROUP BY host
ORDER BY host;
```
Results: host-a 110ms n=15k, host-b 130ms n=9k. Console merged p95 shows ~240ms — looks wrong.
Sam: If merge is doing something like max(p95) or double-counting when fallback forms a separate group you can end up with an arithmetic artifact. Our intended merge is global tdigest on raw samples but some dashboards use per-bucket tdigest merge which depends on consistent provenance.
Jordan: We need to know whether this is a telemetry bug or a routing policy causing true tail shift. How quickly can we check raw samples?
Mike: I'll spin a quick export of raw latencies for the last 20 minutes and compute a single-tdigest p95, then compare. If raw p95 ~120-130 then dashboard merge is the bug. If raw p95 ~240 then routing changed real tail.
deploy-bot: routing-policy: add-fallback-quantized applied to cluster-prod at 1728888820 (by Sam).
Emily: One more datapoint — endpoint breakdown in the console shows a small-but-present `sample_origin` tag on ~40% of the rows marked `fallback`. The top-level view's legend doesn't surface that tag so people won't notice.
Sam: Ok that explains it — fallback samples are getting their own bucket and the top-level merge is accidentally including them twice because of a tag normalization mismatch.
Jordan: Action items: 1) Mike to verify raw-sample global p95; 2) Mike to push dashboard toggle to use single-tdigest merge_mode; 3) Emily to add provenance badge "includes fallback" on top-level panels; 4) Sam to follow up on routing tag normalization bug and revert if necessary.
Mike: I'll do a quick PR for the merge_mode toggle and add sample-count next to each pctl. Small UI change, should be fine for hotfix.
Emily: Also propose we add a tooltip explaining "merge semantics: per-bucket vs global-tdigest" — docs team has been asking for better observability language anyway.
Sam: I'll open an internal bug for the tag normalization and link this thread.
Jordan: Thanks team. After PR goes in can someone confirm that top-level p95 and endpoint breakdown converge (within 5-10ms) and that n counts are consistent? If not, we'll rollback the fallback.
Mike: Will post results here when done. ETA ~25m.
Jordan: :thumbsup:
Mike: PR merged to staging (small toggle + sample-count). Staging raw p95 compute = 125ms, staging merged dashboard = 127ms.
Emily: Nice. Can we push the toggle to prod as feature-flagged first?
Sam: Agreed. I'll hold rollback plan but we can feature-flag. Opening canary to 10% now.
deploy-bot: deploy: prod-dashboard-config updated (feature-flag:tdigest-merge=true) at 1728888904
Mike: After feature-flag on prod, observed: top-level p95 = 128ms, endpoint breakdown p95 host-a=110ms host-b=130ms. Sample counts align.
Jordan: Closing loop — looks like it was a merge-semantic/telemetry mismatch, not a catastrophic routing tail. Thanks everyone. Let's track followups in ENG-8942 (docs + tag-normalize).
